title: Why every flow at 06:00 stops scaling
description: A 24-second explanation of concurrency saturation, queue growth, cascading failure, and staggered recovery.

accessibility.label: Animated pipeline showing flows entering a scheduler, filling twenty execution slots, queueing, failing, and recovering after staggered scheduling
accessibility.longDescription: Ten flows fit within execution capacity. As fifty and then more than two hundred sources target 06:00, capacity fills, a queue grows, timeouts retry together, and failures cascade. Staggered schedules, backoff with jitter, and failure isolation restore stable throughput.

scenes.title: Ten flows
scenes.narration: With ten sources, every flow can start at six and finish smoothly inside the available execution slots.

scenes.title: Fifty flows
scenes.narration: At fifty sources, the same convenient start time creates competition: the slots fill and a queue begins to form.

scenes.title: Collision
scenes.narration: Beyond two hundred sources, the six o'clock spike overwhelms every execution slot at once.

scenes.title: Queue growth
scenes.displayText: Waiting time eats the timeout budget
scenes.narration: The queue keeps growing, so each connector starts later and has less time left to finish before its timeout.

scenes.title: Cascade
scenes.narration: Timed-out flows all retry together, turning one bottleneck into a cascade of failures across the estate.

scenes.title: Stagger
scenes.narration: Dependency-aware staggering replaces the single spike with staggered start waves, and the queue starts to drain.

scenes.title: Isolate
scenes.narration: Backoff with jitter spreads the remaining retries, while circuit breakers isolate the few unhealthy sources.

scenes.title: Stable
scenes.displayText: Bounded work, visible failures, steady output
scenes.narration: The system now runs within capacity, keeps the few remaining failures visible, and delivers validated output on time.

reducedMotionSteps: At 10 sources, all scheduled work fits within the 20 available execution slots.
At 50 sources about 25 jobs queue; beyond 200 sources the 06:00 queue dominates the run window and timeouts begin.
Timed-out flows retry at the same moment, amplifying the bottleneck into a cascade of roughly 85 simultaneous failures.
Staggered start times, backoff with jitter, and circuit breakers drain the queue and restore bounded, stable execution.
